text:
Seattle and Calgary both play on a day's rest, and both are coming off close-to-opposite results. The Kraken beat Toronto 5-4 on Brandon Montour's goal with 0:33 left, though they're still without Jared McCann (lower body, ESPN's estimated return Jan 2). In the two games since he went out, Jordan Eberle has moved beside Matty Beniers and Berkly Catton's usual linemates, and Beniers has taken a spot on the first power-play unit. The Flames lost 4-0 in Edmonton to end a four-game winning streak, and they're missing Samuel Honzek. These two met twice this month, and Seattle won the first 6-1.

Our numbers see an even game (SEA 3.02 expected goals, CGY 2.94). Expected goals measure the quality of chances. Calgary has the better five-on-five share (47% to 44%), but Seattle's results are running ahead of its chances, and the Flames take 4.6 penalties a game. In net, Philipp Grubauer is projected for Seattle at +1.3 goals saved above expected this season, while Dustin Wolf is at -8.6 after a rough 2025-26 start, and he was also below expected last year (-2.8).

Eberle (30% to score) and Joel Farabee (28%), both top power-play options, are worth watching. As Hockey Writers put it, Farabee has been "Excelling in Blake Coleman's Absence." Our under-the-radar picks are Calgary's Morgan Frost, whose dangerous shots rate 23% to score, and Matt Coronato, 58% for a point.
